title: Private product PRD - audit, approval gates, customer-managed networking (draft)
body:
Purpose
This is an early draft PRD capturing product requirements and design notes for three related Private product features we must deliver to satisfy enterprise and regulated customers: (1) robust, customer-configurable audit logs; (2) approval gates for sensitive operations and model rollouts; (3) first-class customer-managed networking options (VPC peering, transit, and on-prem VPN).

Context / motivation
- Customers deploying Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) are asking for auditable, tamper-evident logs with long retention options and easy SIEM exports for SOC2/HIPAA audits.
- Several customers operate in regulated verticals and require explicit approval gates before model changes or access changes reach production (e.g., model pin bumps, quantization toggles).
- Networking must support customer-managed controls: private peering, customer-provided NAT, strict egress controls, and optional air-gapped on-prem packaging.
- These three areas intersect: approval decisions and network events must be captured in the audit stream; audit streams must be exportable to customer SIEMs over private networking paths.

Goals (MVP)
- Audit logs: structured, append-only event stream with per-customer encryption, configurable retention (30d/90d/1y/forever), and exports to S3, Splunk HEC, and syslog/CEF endpoints. Support query by request-id, user, model, route, and action.
- Approval gates: admin-configurable policies that can require manual approval for a set of operations and automatic webhooks for external approvers. Approvals must be logged, versioned, and reversible.
- Customer-managed networking: documented VPC peering and Transit Gateway patterns for AWS, GCP Shared VPC patterns, and VPN setup for on-prem packages. Enable optional egress blocking and allow customers to route audit exports over private links.

Out of scope (for first release)
- Full UI for complex approval workflows (we'll ship a simple admin console + webhook API first).
- Native Splunk app (we'll provide ingest formats and sample dashboards).
- Advanced tamper-resistant ledger (blockchain-style) — append-only with cryptographic signatures is planned but not in MVP.

Functional requirements
1) Audit logs
  - R1.1: Every privileged operation (model deploy/promotion, config change, approval decision, user grant/revoke, infra changes) must emit a structured audit event.
  - R1.2: Events must include at minimum: timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, user_id (or service principal), request_id, operation_type, resource, old_value, new_value, result (success/fail), actor_ip, region, and metadata (freeform map).
  - R1.3: Audit events must be persisted locally for 30 days by default; retention configurable per-tenant via console or API (30d/90d/365d/forever).
  - R1.4: Support push exports to customer endpoints: S3 (bucket + prefix), Splunk HEC token + endpoint, syslog/CEF over TLS, and generic HTTPS webhook with retries and DLQ.
  - R1.5: Logs must be encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS key option (bring-your-own-key).
  - R1.6: Provide a lightweight query API for audit events (filter by time, tenant, user, operation, request_id) and an export job to fetch larger slices.
  - R1.7: Deliver sample Splunk/Datadog dashboards + ingestion examples.

2) Approval gates
  - R2.1: Define a policy model: operations -> scope (global/org/project/model) -> requirement (none/manual-approve/webhook-approval/2fa).
  - R2.2: Admins can create rules via Console / API. Each rule has: name, scope, operations list, approver group (email list or SSO group), timeout, and escalate policy.
  - R2.3: Manual approval workflow: when an operation requiring approval is attempted, create an Approval Request (AR) with details and notify approvers via email + optional webhook. AR must be reviewable in Console with comment history and attachments (e.g., evals).
  - R2.4: Approvals must be cryptographically signed and recorded into the audit stream (linkable by AR id).
  - R2.5: Support automated gates driven by webhook response (e.g., external policy engine returns allow/deny). Webhook must return decision within configurable timeout; otherwise default deny or fallback policy.
  - R2.6: Provide API endpoints to list pending ARs, approve/deny with reason, and to fetch approval history.

3) Customer-managed networking
  - R3.1: Document and automate (where possible) VPC peering setup (AWS) and Shared VPC connectors (GCP). Provide Terraform snippets for customer infra.
  - R3.2: Support routing audit export traffic over customer-managed endpoints (S3 via VPC endpoints, Splunk HEC over private connectivity, or syslog via VPN).
  - R3.3: For on-prem customers: support an OVA/docker bundle that can forward audit logs to customer SIEM on-prem (with offline/queueing support).
  - R3.4: Provide network hardening checklist for customers (restrict outbound to known Redwood IPs, egress firewall rules, KMS connectivity).
  - R3.5: Allow customers to bring their own NAT/Egress and require egress IP whitelisting for control-plane callbacks.

Non-functional requirements
- NFR1: Latency — approval gating should not add more than 200ms to non-blocking ops; blocking ops will wait for human approval (SLA for webhook responses: configurable, default 30s).
- NFR2: Reliability — audit export retries with exponential backoff, DLQ storage for failed deliveries up to 7 days.
- NFR3: Security — default encryption-in-transit + at-rest; BYOK option for audit store KMS; HSM/KMS integration docs.
- NFR4: Scalability — system must support sustained 50k events/min across fleet for large customers; backpressure mechanisms and batching.
- NFR5: Compliance — features must support customers’ SOC2/HIPAA evidence needs (exportable reports, retention proofs).

UX / Console flows (MVP)
- Admin -> Security -> Audit Settings: retention dropdown, KMS key ARN input, export endpoints list (add/verify).
- Admin -> Security -> Approval Policies: create policy wizard (scope, operations, approvers, mode), list of pending ARs with quick-approve.
- Operator experience when performing gated action: modal shows policy required, summary of pending AR, link to create justification and attach evaluation artifacts, submit for approval -> status page updates.

Data & event format (proposal)
- Top-level JSON event: {
  "ts": "2025-11-01T14:23:12Z",
  "tenant_id": "acct_abc123",
  "request_id": "req_xxx-yyy",
  "actor": "user:alice@acme.com",
  "operation": "model.promote",
  "resource": "models/experiment-45",
  "old": "{\"tag\":\"canary\"}",
  "new": "{\"tag\":\"production\"}",
  "result": "success",
  "ctx": {"latency_ms": 123, "node": "us-west-2-a"},
  "signature": "base64sig..."
}
- Signature: HMAC-SHA256 or RSA signature depending on BYOK selection. Note: signing strategy needs design.

Operational playbook (SRE notes)
- On export failure: queue event -> exponential retry -> push to DLQ S3/Blob -> alert on sustained DLQ growth.
- Key rotation: support rekeying for BYOK without losing verify trail (keep old public keys for verification window).
- Incident response: if audit pipeline fails, surface a degraded banner in Console and provide downloadable local archive for customers.

Acceptance criteria (sample)
- AC1: Simulate a tenant performing 100k privileged ops over 24h, verify 99.9% events persisted and exported to S3 with no loss.
- AC2: Create an approval policy that requires manual approval for model.promote; attempt promote -> approval request created, approver receives webhook/email, approval recorded and action completes.
- AC3: Customer sets up VPC peering and configures S3 endpoints; audit export over VPC endpoint completes and is visible in customer bucket.

Open questions / design decisions
- Q1: Signing model for approvals and logs: HMAC per-tenant vs RSA per-tenant keypair + KMS? Tradeoffs: HMAC simpler, RSA better public verification.
- Q2: Retention billing model: bill for storage used for export retention? or include X days in plan and charge overage? Need finance input.
- Q3: Approval UX: do we support multi-approver quorum (e.g., 2-of-3) in MVP or keep single-approver first?
- Q4: On-prem bundle telemetry: allowed phone-home metrics vs fully air-gapped mode (compliance asks for both). Need legal guidance.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Customers might treat exported logs as the single source of truth; if we reformat events we risk breaking dashboards. Mitigation: provide stable schema v1 and publishing deprecation schedule.
- Risk: Approval webhook latency/availability causing blocked operations. Mitigation: configurable fallback policies and local cache of last-known decisions for safe defaults.

Milestones / proposed timeline (quarterly stretches)
- Q4 2025: Audit event infra, basic console retention & exports, sample dashboard artifacts.
- Q1 2026: BYOK for audit store, S3 + Splunk export hardened, VPC peering automation docs and Terraform snippets.
- Q2 2026: Approval gates API + Console flow, webhook integrations, AR UX improvements.

Implementation notes / infra implications (engineering hints)
- Leverage existing logging pipeline but add explicit audit topic with stricter guarantees (e.g., exactly-once append into tenant partition).
- Use Kafka/Managed streaming to buffer events, redact PII at ingestion based on tenant policy, and support per-tenant encryption.
- Export workers should be zonal with leader election per tenant export job to avoid duplicate deliveries.

Next steps / owners
- Draft detailed event schema (owner: Juniper) — due 2025-09-18
- Security review of BYOK and signing model (owner: Ravi) — due 2025-09-25
- Console mockups for Approval Requests list + AR detail (owner: Clara) — draft 2025-09-22
- Infra spike: proof-of-concept export to S3 over VPC endpoint (owner: Mateo) — prototype 2025-10-06

Notes to self
- Keep audit schema compact (avoid embedding large eval artifacts — instead reference artifact id).
- Talk to GTM about packaging this as a compliance add-on (pricing).

References
- Internal confluence: PRD-private-deployments-overview (link in header)
- Slack thread: #enterprise-onboarding (see pinned messages 2025-08-11)
- Jira: INF-2431 (audit exports backlog), SEC-987 (BYOK security questions)

Unresolved (parking lot)
- Long-term: tamper-evident ledger and public key verification for customers wanting independent verification.
- Long-term: native SIEM connectors and alerting rules library.

End of draft.

Feedback welcome — ping me in #product-private or add comments in Confluence page.
